# `Browser.Geolocation`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Geolocation — read the device's location over `Ipe.Js` ports.

A first-party proof of the per-capability web mechanism spanning BOTH port
directions: an outbound `JsCmd` requests a position (one-shot or a continuous
watch), and an inbound `JsMsg` carries the reply — a decoded `Coords` or one of
three enumerated denials. Both cross the same seal codec and fail-closed port
discipline as every other port; there is no second transport.

Importing this reserved `Ipe.Browser.<Api>` module discloses
`js-port:geolocation` (import-derived, keyed on the canonical path, alias-immune);
only the top-level app's `[capabilities] accepts` set can grant it.

The two layers:

  * `Ipe.Browser.Geolocation.Internals` publishes the closed outbound/inbound
    ADTs and the full `Options` surface (`enableHighAccuracy` / `timeout` /
    `maximumAge`) for a caller that needs every knob.
  * this module is the high-level layer: `current` / `watch` / `stopWatching`
    with sane defaults, and `positions` — the inbound subscription that folds
    the narrow `JsMsg` into a typed `Result Error Coords`. The inbound `case`
    is EXHAUSTIVE over `Position` / `Denied` / `Unavailable` / `Timeout`: a host
    permission denial becomes a typed `Err`, never a silently dropped variant.

The one-shot `current` is shaped as an outbound `Cmd`, not a `Task Error Coords`:
the raw `Ipe.Js` transport has no request→reply correlation kernel, so a
`Task`-shaped one-shot cannot be spelled over it today. The reply to `current`
arrives on the same `positions` subscription as a watch's. Closing that gap
(a correlated port→`Task` bridge) is tracked — it needs a new backend kernel and
a security-soundness review of the JS boundary, not a stdlib-only change.

## `Coords`

A device position: WGS-84 latitude/longitude in degrees, accuracy in metres.

## `current`

```ipe
current : Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`current` — request the device's location ONCE.

Outbound `Cmd` over the raw port transport with sane defaults (low accuracy, no
timeout, a fresh fix). The served JS handler reaches
`navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition`; the reply — a `Coords` or a typed
denial — arrives on the `positions` subscription.

Importing this module discloses `js-port:geolocation`; the app must grant it
with `accepts = [ JsPort Geolocation ]` under [capabilities] in package.ipe.

## `watch`

```ipe
watch : Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`watch` — begin a CONTINUOUS position stream.

Outbound `Cmd` that arms `navigator.geolocation.watchPosition`; each new fix (or
a denial) is delivered on the `positions` subscription until `stopWatching`.

## `stopWatching`

```ipe
stopWatching : Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`stopWatching` — end the continuous stream started by `watch`.

## `positions`

```ipe
positions : (Result Error Coords -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`positions toMsg` — the inbound subscription, wired in `subscriptions`.

The decoder IS the security gate: every inbound value runs through the total,
bounded seal decoder for the narrow `JsMsg`; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is folded EXHAUSTIVELY into a
`Result Error Coords` — a `Position` becomes `Ok`, and each of the three denial
variants becomes a typed `Err`, so no denial can be silently swallowed.
